claims: President Donald Trump fired Pam Bondi as United States Attorney General as of April 2, 2026.
Pam Bondi's tenure as United States Attorney General was 14 months.
Trump cited frustration over Pam Bondi's handling of the Jeffrey Epstein files in firing her.
Trump cited Pam Bondi's failure to aggressively investigate political opponents in firing her.
Pam Bondi is transitioning to a private-sector role.
Pam Bondi is replaced by Acting Attorney General Todd Blanche.
Bondi faced bipartisan criticism for her management of the investigation into Jeffrey Epstein.
The criticism of Bondi included delays in releasing Epstein files.
The criticism of Bondi included issues with redacting victim names.
Congress voted to subpoena Bondi over the handling of the Epstein files.
Trump was reportedly unsatisfied with Bondi's performance as the nation's top law enforcement officer.
Bondi stated she would work to transition her office to Deputy Attorney General Todd Blanche.
Bondi is the second major official to be removed from the Trump administration in early 2026.
Homeland Security Secretary Kristi Noem was ousted from the Trump administration in early 2026.
